1: Inside a Chinese prison, a man disguised as a medic attempts to break a woman out of her cell.
2: Although he triggers a blackout and comes within inches of escaping, the man—American CIA agent Tom Bishop—ultimately finds himself surrounded at gunpoint.
3: Now, his fate rests entirely in the hands of a veteran operative just one day away from retirement.
4: As Chinese officers monitor the prison from the control room, tension mounts among the medical staff.
5: With a prisoner being wheeled out under a sheet, he has only seven minutes left.
6: As alarms blare through the dark corridors, Bishop shines his flashlight and heads toward the cell.
7: A pre-dawn phone call from Duncan at the Hong Kong station delivers a coded warning that a Boy Scout is in trouble.
8: Nathan Muir arrives for work at CIA headquarters on the final day of his thirty-year career.
9: Muir exchanges warm smiles and greetings with his colleagues at headquarters, but his mind is entirely consumed by the cable from Hong Kong.
10: Then, his colleague Harker approaches him and demands the files on Tom Bishop, the operative Muir trained.
11: While packing up his belongings, Muir flips through a Bahamas travel brochure, dreaming of his post-retirement getaway.
12: Sensing that something is amiss, Muir hands a burn bag to his secretary, Gladys.
13: In the operations room, news broadcasts report on the President's upcoming visit to China.
14: Summoned to the conference room, Muir finds top CIA officials already gathered there.
15: During the high-level meeting chaired by Director Troy Folger, news breaks that Bishop has been captured in China on espionage charges.
16: However, with the President's visit to China just a week away, the CIA has no intention of rescuing Bishop and plans to quietly abandon him instead.
17: When the executives question Muir about Bishop's past, Muir recalls the day they first met in Vietnam in 1975.
18: When his helicopter touches down at a camp in Vietnam, Muir learns that the sniper he was looking for has already been killed in action.
19: In need of a replacement sniper, Muir is introduced to a young sergeant named Tom Bishop.
20: Seeing a cocky yet ideal soldier in him, Muir assigns him the mission of assassinating an enemy general.
21: Just as Bishop takes aim at the target, however, a friendly helicopter blocks his line of sight, throwing the operation into chaos.
22: Once the helicopter clears out of the way, Bishop finally makes the shot and escapes the jungle carrying his wounded partner on his back.
23: As a helicopter flies low over the burning jungle, Muir shouts at the pilot to turn back and pick up the two men.
24: Back in the conference room, however, the executives begin painting Bishop as a reckless killing machine.
25: Meanwhile, Gladys calls to warn Muir that someone is already ransacking his office.
26: Muir excuses himself from the meeting and hurries back to his office.
27: Returning to his office, Muir decides to leak the news of Bishop's arrest in China to the press through his old reporter friend, Digger Gibson.
28: At that very moment in the Chinese prison, Bishop is being subjected to brutal torture.
29: Borrowing a phone in a colleague's office, Muir sets his covert rescue operation in motion.
30: Muir's flashback continues to Berlin, where he tracked down Bishop just before his discharge and recruited him into the CIA.
31: On the stairs at a Christmas party, Muir offers Bishop a chance to become a CIA operative.
32: From that day on, Bishop undergoes grueling training in the art of observing people, lying, and extracting information.
33: Practicing his observation skills on people in the streets, Bishop rapidly hones his craft.
34: Along the way, Muir imparts the ironclad rules of espionage to him.
35: Bishop proves to be a natural-born operative, even convincing an East German defector to return as a double agent.
36: The executives then begin grilling Muir about Operation Rodeo, a Berlin mission in which Bishop was involved.
37: Bishop's first mission is to smuggle an East German official named Schmidt across the border, but Muir abruptly calls from a party and orders him to abandon the man.
38: Pounding on a restroom wall to catch his breath, Bishop realizes that enemy lookouts are already closing in outside.
39: In the end, Bishop drags the wailing Schmidt out of the car and leaves him behind.
40: When the two men confront each other on a rooftop and Bishop demands answers, Muir coldly tells him that Schmidt was merely bait from the start.
41: Leaving Bishop sitting there in stunned disbelief, Muir silently walks toward the edge of the roof.
42: Two months later, Anne Cathcart, a double agent at the embassy, is found dead in an East German hotel.
43: In the conference room, it is revealed that the operation Bishop had been targeting was Side Show, a covert mission to wiretap the Chinese government.
44: Just then, the story Muir leaked breaks on the news, but the CIA immediately counters by claiming that Bishop died a year ago.
45: When the meeting takes a brief recess, Muir casually packs up his things and heads out to avoid suspicion, while Gladys sees him off with a wistful look.
46: With every official avenue of rescue blocked, Muir resorts to his final option.
47: Collapsed on the floor of the Chinese prison, Bishop is rapidly running out of time.
48: Flashing a knowing smile at Harker, Muir is already preparing his next move.
49: Visiting a colleague, Muir discovers that a squadron of U.S. military helicopters is on standby at Penghu Island near China.
50: After slipping past Harker's surveillance, Muir has Gladys gather satellite and video analysis data of the prison.
51: Returning to the conference room, Muir reveals the name of the woman Bishop was trying to rescue.
52: In war-torn Beirut in 1985, Bishop goes undercover as a war photojournalist on a mission to assassinate a terrorist leader.
53: Through the nights in Beirut, Bishop mingles with informants at a bar to solidify his cover.
54: Through Elizabeth, a relief worker at a local refugee camp, Bishop gets close to the target's personal physician.
55: Posing as a journalist chasing news on the Israeli military, Bishop exchanges intelligence every morning beside the rooftop birdcages.
56: One day, Muir shows up in Beirut in person, and Bishop surprises him with a birthday gift flown in all the way from London.
57: Walking past wrecked cars toward a seaside restaurant, the two men share a rare moment of laughter.
58: As the two watch the harbor through binoculars from a rooftop, the Sheik arrives in Beirut by motorboat.
59: Just in case, Muir meets with a Lebanese militia to set up a backup plan.
60: Presenting proof that the death of the doctor's parents was no accident, Bishop offers him a chance for revenge.
61: Upon receiving a report that Bishop is spending every night with Elizabeth, Muir's eyes turn cold.
62: Learning of the relationship between Bishop and Elizabeth, Muir unceremoniously crashes their dinner.
63: Suspecting Elizabeth of being a spy, Muir corners Bishop and pressures him to end things.
64: Digging into Elizabeth's past, Muir discovers she belonged to a human rights group that bombed a Chinese government building in London.
65: Bishop hands the doctor a poisoned stethoscope containing a toxin lethal enough to kill within twelve hours from just half a drop.
66: With four days left until the assassination, Muir and Bishop anxiously await the fateful day.
67: Ultimately, Bishop reveals his real name to Elizabeth.
68: That morning, upon hearing news that the refugee camp has been bombed, Elizabeth takes the doctor and leaves right away.
69: On the day of the assassination, when the doctor disappears with Elizabeth, Muir triggers his backup plan—a militia car bomb.
70: Bishop speeds across the market in his car to forcibly bring the doctor back from the camp.
71: Bishop barely manages to send the doctor in to see the target, but just then, the militia's bomb truck hurtles straight into the building.
72: The building housing the target collapses in a massive explosion, blanketing the streets in bodies and smoke.
73: Covered in blood, Bishop wanders dazedly through the horrific wreckage.
74: When the two men cross paths at the airport, Bishop turns his back on Muir.
75: After Elizabeth leaves Beirut, Bishop sits alone in an empty room and reads the note she left behind.
76: Leaving only a single note behind, Elizabeth vanishes from Beirut.
77: Back at CIA headquarters in the present, the meeting is adjourned until the next morning for a White House briefing, and Muir, left alone, makes up his mind.
78: Sneaking a look at a top-secret document on Folger's desk, Muir confirms that the CIA has decided to abandon Bishop for good and liquidates his entire life's retirement savings.
79: Back in the conference room, the executives have already made the final decision to let Bishop be executed.
80: Contacting his old colleague Duncan in Hong Kong—who had called him at dawn—Muir arranges a thirty-minute blackout around the prison and spends the night forging an operational directive.
81: Tracking Muir's phone records, Harker slowly closes in on his scheme.
82: The price for the blackout is $282,000, the entirety of Muir's retirement savings.
83: At the meeting the next morning, Harker confronts Muir with evidence of his suspicious wire transfer.
84: Harker also reveals that Gibson, the reporter to whom Muir leaked the story, is actually a British intelligence operative.
85: However, Muir calmly bluffs his way out, claiming he was merely using spy satellites to scout beachfront property for his retirement.
86: Muir then confesses a truth that even Bishop didn't know: that he himself was the one who had Elizabeth thrown into the Chinese prison.
87: Just then, a phone call comes through from Commander Wiley on Penghu Island.
88: The executives assume the call is merely about dinner plans with his wife, but at that exact moment, the lights go out at Su Chou prison.
89: In the darkness of Su Chou prison, the footsteps of soldiers echo closer.
90: Special forces storm the dark cell and load a bloodied Bishop and Elizabeth onto a helicopter.
91: Muir signs his non-disclosure exit papers and walks out of headquarters as if nothing happened.
92: Aboard the helicopter, Bishop realizes that the rescue mission—"Operation Dinner Out"—was named after the very birthday gift he had given Muir in Beirut.
93: By the time Harker finally pieces everything together in the conference room at headquarters, Muir has already driven off calmly into the distance.
94: This was director Tony Scott's *Spy Game*, a film that drew buzz for pairing two generations of stars, Robert Redford and Brad Pitt.
95: Seeing a veteran agent give up his entire life savings to save his protégé, would you have made the same choice if you were in Muir's shoes—let us know in the comments!
